Li-Lee coherent multi-population model

Source: R/model-multipop.R
li_lee.Rd

Joint model for several strata (for example women and men, or regions) whose forecasts do not diverge in the long run (Li and Lee 2005): log m[x,t,i] = a[x,i] + B[x] K[t] + b[x,i] k[t,i]. The common factor B K is a Lee-Carter model of the pooled rates (sum of deaths over sum of exposures, SVD with K refitted to the total deaths of each year); the stratum factors b k are the first ratio_order components of an SVD of the residuals of each stratum.

Usage

li_lee(ratio_order = 1, common_by = NULL, jump_off = c("fitted", "observed"))

Arguments

ratio_order

Number of stratum-specific factors.

common_by

Stratum variable(s) defining groups with their own common factor.

jump_off

"fitted" (forecasts start from the fitted rates of the last year) or "observed" (forecasts are multiplied by the ratio of observed to fitted rates in the last year, per age and stratum; Lee and Miller 2001). With few factors per stratum the fitted rates of the last year can be far from the observed ones; the observed jump-off then avoids a step between the last observed and the first forecast year.

Value

A model specification.

Details

With common_by (for example "sex"), li_lee() fits one common factor per level of that stratum variable (women and men each with their own trend), and the other strata (for example regions and deprivation quintiles) deviate from their group's common factor. If the data carry a hierarchy (see mt_aggregate_strata()), the common factors are estimated from the bottom strata only, so aggregates are not counted twice.

The common period index follows a random walk with drift (with drift uncertainty) and the stratum-specific indexes k[t,i] follow AR(1) processes, so the differences between strata stay bounded. Two choices of this package differ from Li and Lee (2005), who model k[t,i] as an AR(1) process with a constant:

  • the AR(1) processes have no constant (intercept): the coefficient is the least-squares estimate through the origin, and the stratum indexes revert to zero, their mean over the fitting period;

  • the AR(1) coefficient is bounded to |phi| <= 0.99, a package-specific safeguard against unit roots and explosive deviations (reference unknown). A warning (class mt_warning_li_lee) names the strata where the bound binds; their deviations then revert very slowly, and the assumption of coherence may not suit them.

Draws include the innovations of all indexes and the drift uncertainty of the common index; a, B, b and the AR(1) coefficients are fixed. Predictive draws (mt_forecast(predictive = TRUE)) add Poisson variation of the deaths given the rates and the exposures, and no other observation noise. If intervals are too narrow on real data, that is a property of the model (see recalibrated(), ensemble(), or overdispersed models such as stanmomo(family = "nb")).

product_ratio(), a Lee-Carter version of the product-ratio method, is deprecated; use coherent_fdm().

References

Li N, Lee R (2005). Coherent mortality forecasts for a group of populations: an extension of the Lee-Carter method. Demography 42(3): 575-594. doi:10.1353/dem.2005.0021

Lee RD, Carter LR (1992). Modeling and forecasting U.S. mortality. Journal of the American Statistical Association 87(419): 659-671.

Lee R, Miller T (2001). Evaluating the performance of the Lee-Carter method for forecasting mortality. Demography 38(4): 537-549.

See also

coherent_fdm() for the product-ratio method.

Examples

x <- mt_example(deaths = "single")
fc <- mt_forecast(mt_fit(li_lee(), x), h = 10, n_draws = 100, seed = 1)
